Following:
 Judgment
This appeal is by the claimants in MVC No.103/2018 on the file of the II Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT, Raichur (for short, 'the Tribunal').

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has awarded a total sum of Rs.16,82,800/- to the claimants as compensation for the demise of Sri Late Venkatesh in a road accident on 07.01.2018.
This accident has occurred when Sri Venkatesh and others were traveling on the motorcycle at about 6.00 p.m. on 07.01.2018.

2. The claimants' entitlement to recover compensation from the respondents, including the insurer,
because of the aforesaid demise in the road accident is not disputed.
The Tribunal has granted a total sum of Rs.16,12,800/- towards loss of dependency and a further sum of Rs.70,000/- towards transportation and funeral expenses, loss of estate and loss of consortium.

The Tribunal has determined loss of NC: 2023:KHC-K:1226-DB dependency taking the notional income of Sri Venkatesh at Rs.8,000/- per month with an addition of 40% towards future prospects and deducting 1/4th towards personal expenses of the deceased and applying the multiplier of '16'
because the deceased was aged 35 years as of the date of the accident.
3.

Sri Sanganagouda V. Biradar, the learned counsel for the appellants, submits that the compensation towards loss of dependency must be recomputed taking a higher monthly income of the deceased and just amount towards loss of consortium.

The learned counsel relies upon Ex.P-8, a certificate issued by M/s. Shree Devishree Traders, Commission Agents and Merchants, Raichur, to contend that the deceased was earning Rs.450/- per day and maintaining a large family comprising of five children.
There is no exaggeration in the appellants claiming monthly income for a sum of Rs.15,000/-.

On the ground of loss of consortium, the learned counsel submits that each of the NC:
2023:KHC-K:1226-DB appellants viz., Sri Venkatesh's wife, four minor children and the dependant mother would be entitled to conventional sum of Rs.40,000/- each.

It is argued on behalf of the Insurer that this Court cannot attach any credence to Ex.P-8 because none is examined to establish the probative value of this certificate even if it could be said that the deceased Sri Venkatesh was indeed the employee with the aforesaid firm.
4. There is considerable force in this opposition, and this Court cannot rely upon the certificate to enhance the compensation.

However, it is undisputed that in the cases of accidents of the year 2018,
notional income is taken at Rs.11,750/- to settle claims.

In this case there are no circumstances that would justify excluding this income, and in fact, this Court is of the considered view that in view of the categorical evidence by the first appellant - the wife of deceased Sri Venkatesh that he was working with M/s. Shree Devishree Traders, Commission Agents and Merchants, Raichur stitching gunny bags and a Hamali and the irrefutable fact that he NC: 2023:KHC-K:1226-DB was supporting a family of six, the monthly income must be taken at Rs.12,000/- with necessary addition of 40%
towards future prospects and deduction of 1/4th towards personal expenses, retaining the multiplier Smt. Pooja And Ors vs Shashiraj Maski And Anr on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102140352/
3 applied by the Tribunal.

sentences.text:
In which event, the appellants will be entitled for compensation towards loss of dependency as calculated hereunder:
Computation of Loss of Dependency Description By the Tribunal By this Court Income `8,000.00 `12,000.00 Addition of such Income at the rate 40% towards `3,200.00 `4,800.00 future prospects Monthly Income with the addition towards `11,200.00 `16,800.00 future prospects
Deduction of 1/4th towards personal `2,800.00 `4,200.00 expenses Monthly income with addition of future `8,400.00 `12,600.00 prospects and deduction towards personal expenses
Income Loss of Dependency `16,12,800.00 `24,19,200.00 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1226-DB 5.
Therefore, the appellants will be entitled for a sum of Rs.24,19,200/- as against the sum of Rs.16,12,800/-.
The appellants are the bereaved widow aged 29 years and four minor children and a dependant mother aged 55 years.
In law, it would be just and proper to award loss of consortium in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each to all of them apart from the conventional heads.

Hence, the total compensation resulting in enhancement would be as under:
The computation of enhancement:
 By Tribunal By this Court  Description Loss of dependency `16,12,800.00 `24,19,200.00 Loss of estate &
 `30,000.00 `30,000.00 funeral expenses Loss of consortium `40,000.00 `2,40,000.00
Total `
Enhancement `10,06,400.00
For the foregoing, the following:

ORDER The appeal is allowed in part modifying the impugned judgment and award dated 19.06.2019 in MVC NC: 2023:KHC-K:1226-DB No.103/2018 on the file of the II Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT, Raichur and granting enhanced compensation of Rs.10,06,400/-.

entities.text: II Additional District and Sessions Judge and MACT, Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This amount of Rs.10,06,400 shall be deposited by the respondent - insurance company with the Tribunal within eight [8] weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment, along with interest at the rate of 6%.

The apportionment of this enhanced compensation amongst the appellants shall be as directed by the Tribunal and the amount payable to the minor appellants' share shall be in deposit until they attain majority.
